evidence.text: The first FY27 guide will carry NASA insourcing at the upper bound already flagged: management said on the 2026-08-11 call that NASA insourcing would cut about 3% of FY27 revenue (up from about 1% a quarter earlier), with 'not all contract actions in hand'. The risk is a NASA cut above the 3% already framed, against a market that expects a near-flat FY27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-10): revenue guide cut and the NASA headwind raised from 1% to 3%; the stock fell 8.22% despite raised EBITDA and EPS guides. Q4 FY25 (2025-11-24), when the first FY26 guide was given: +18.25%. So this line has moved the stock both ways by 8-18 points.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The 3% is public and the stock has fallen since. Not priced: whether 3% is still the number after NASA's plan firmed and KBR booked a debooking. evidence.text: The FY26 guide implies Q4 revenue of only +3% to +7% over Q3 ($3.595-3.745B against $3.49B). Last year Q4 rose about 10% over Q3 ($3.56B to $3.92B) and beat consensus by $310M on government fiscal year-end volume. Management also attributed about $175M of FY26 revenue to protest and procurement delays, and the main protests have since been resolved in Amentum's favour: COSMOS and CMOE II in Q3, and GAO denied HII's protest of a ~$708M Navy task order on 2026-11-05. Q4 revenue at or above the top of the implied range is plausible against a $3.66B consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue is the line this stock trades on. Q3 FY26: an EPS beat ($0.67 vs $0.61) with a revenue miss ($3.49B vs ~$3.58-3.6B) sold off 8.2%. Q4 FY25: revenue beat by $310M, together with the first FY26 guide, +18.25%. Q1 FY26: revenue -5% (shutdown, JV transitions), -12.38%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the midpoint of the implied guide, so the Street has not modelled last year's Q4 seasonality on top of it. If it had, the $3.66B consensus would sit near the $3.75B top, and Chartmill's $3.77B shows at least one dissenting estimate. This is inference from seasonality, not a company number, and last year's Q4 included divested and deconsolidated work.
evidence.independence: Q3 FY26 release for the $175M delay and protest resolutions: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002011286/000162828026055294/exhibit991-august102026.htm. HII protest denied (2026-11-05), from the GAO protest search via https://www.gao.gov/products/b-424562,b-424562.2. Both are separate documents from the FY25 Q4 release this finding is sized on.

evidence.text: Holding the FY26 FCF guide of $525-575M needs Q4 free cash flow of $312-362M (YTD $213M through Q3). That is 20-39% above Q4 FY25's $261M, on a name with 3.0x net leverage. YTD FCF is also behind last year (FY25 YTD through Q3 was about $255M = $516M full year less $261M in Q4). A low-end or missed FCF print keeps leverage near 3x and slows deleveraging.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY25 (strong $261M FCF, FY25 $516M): +18.25%, though the guide was also given that day. No clean isolated FCF reaction in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Previews focus on revenue and the FY27 guide; the Earnings Whispers preview does not mention the Q4 cash requirement. This lands inside a guide the company reaffirmed in August knowing the YTD figure, which is why it is sized small. If the market doubted the cash, the skew would read the same, so this does not separate.
evidence.independence: FY25 Q4 FCF $261M and full-year $516M from the FY25 Q4 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2011286/000162828025053839/exhibit991-november242025.htm. Same company, two documents.

evidence.text: September 2026 was the warmest September on record for the contiguous US (NOAA, reported 2026-10-08) and October 2026 the fourth-warmest October, with the Ohio Valley third-warmest. Net: Q3 comp is more likely in the bottom half of the 1-3% guide than above the ~2%+ the street usually carries.

evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down ~21% since the print and puts are bid. What would differ if fully priced: consensus revenue would sit at the guide midpoint ($2.98B), not the top ($3.00B). It has not moved there, while EPS estimates were cut.
evidence.independence: TJX (2026-11-18) said 'unseasonably warm weather in the U.S. and Canada has been holding back consumer demand in some categories' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000109198/000010919826000058/tjxq3fy27earningspressrele.htm); Climate Central October 2026 briefing, fourth-warmest October (https://www.climatecentral.org/climate-briefings/october-2026); Canada Goose said October comps stayed negative on warm weather (https://retail-insider.com/?p=211165). evidence.text: On the Aug 27 call the CFO said the Q3-to-date comp trend was 'within our 1% to 3% Q3 comp guidance range', with August 'our toughest monthly compare in the third quarter' and compares easing in September and October. evidence.text: Every direct peer and counterparty that reported after HPE's 2026-09-02 print beat and raised. HPE's Q4 revenue consensus of $14.40B sits at the guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (Sept 2026) was a record revenue beat with raised FY26 and FY27 guides. Premarket it traded about -5% on supply constraints (finviz 388456) and the baseline records +5.04% for the full window. Q2 FY26 (June) was +19.47%. Beats on this name have been bought on net, but not reliably.
evidence.why_not_priced: HPE fell about 20.5% in the month to Nov 12 while the S&P 500 lost 1.6% (Trefis, 2026-11-13). The prints above landed in that window and did not stop the slide. If the market had carried peer demand into HPE's quarter, the stock would not be 35% off its high at about 10.8x forward earnings into a print guided +49% y/y. The selling is a sector and macro derating (AI capex fears, midterm regulation worries), not a read of HPE's line items. Partly priced: these are public, widely read prints.
evidence.independence: Separate companies and separate documents. Arista: https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20261103862513/arista-networks-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results (2026-11-03). If the orders were priced as FY27 revenue, the forward multiple would not have compressed to about 10.8x. Partly priced, because the orders are public.

evidence.text: FAA ground stop on Nov 13, 2026 (17 of 22 en route centers affected) was traced to newly installed HPE Juniper routers. The FAA paused new Juniper installs and disabled a router feature. Thirteen Democratic senators (Senate Commerce, Cantwell) asked on Nov 17 for the deployment to be suspended: 3,648 routers are slated, 400 installed, 69 operational. Root cause is unresolved and HPE says the routers 'functioned as configured by the installer'. This will be a call topic and a headline risk for the Networking segment the bull case rests on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance. Reaction so far: about -2.3% on Nov 17 (goldesel.de, in EUR), then +3.9% premarket on Nov 18 when HPE defended the routers and Nvidia beat (finviz 424517).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The dollar exposure is small: one FAA program, through L3Harris, against $2.9B a quarter of Networking revenue that is growing high-teens to low-20s. What is not priced is whether management quantifies it or whether other federal buyers pause. Net of the rest of Networking it is small.
evidence.independence: https://keyt.com/news/national-world/cnn-national/2026/11/17/faa-pauses-juniper-router-installations-after-nationwide-ground-stop/ (CNN via KEYT, 2026-11-17) confirms the pause.

evidence.why_not_priced: Both facts are public. But the stock has fallen about 23% from its $26.90 high and 10% in 20 days while this cash was being paid, so the price is not trading on it. evidence.independence: Shares the 'Chinese IoT exporters had a strong Q3' theme with the Espressif finding but from a different layer (device makers vs chip supplier) and different documents.

evidence.text: Semiconductor and memory input-cost inflation compressed Tuya's PaaS gross margin to 46.8% in Q2 2026 from 48.7% (overall 46.3% vs 48.4%), the company said costs would stabilise only over the next two to three quarters, and smart-home peers (Ecovacs) blamed Q3 profit declines on memory-chip prices, so Q3 gross margin likely stays below the 48.3% of Q3 2025.

evidence.independence: Transcript says most Q2 pricing passed higher input costs through and costs should stabilise in 2-3 quarters (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262129870-tradingkey); same company source family as the release.

evidence.text: Tuya declared a cash dividend with both its Q2 2025 results (Aug 2025, ~$33M) and its Q4 2025 results (Mar 2026, $0.0605/ADS, ~$37M), but the Q2 2026 release (Aug 24, 2026) carried no dividend declaration, breaking the semi-annual pattern, while the equity now trades below its ~$976M cash pile (market cap ~$895M at $1.46 on ~613.3M shares); a capital-return announcement with Q3 (dividend or buyback) is possible but not signalled.

If the market expected a Q3 capital return the stock would not be making new lows into the print. Conversely, if Tuya has moved to one annual dividend with Q4 results, nothing happens on this print, which is why the central size is small.
evidence.independence: Dividend history from the Q2 2025 release title (https://tuya.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tuya-reports-second-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and) and the Q4 2025 release (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/tuya-reports-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-declaration-of-cash-dividend-20260302); share count from Tuya's HKEX monthly return (https://www.itiger.com/news/1171769739).
